items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: And in the band was... Johnny Fisher... and myself on snare drum.

ctx.x: How many of those bands would really swing there in the Rex parade?

Well, the Fish's Band was the only band in the whole parade that swang. Incidentally, it was all white bands. The Fish's Band was the only band in the parade that swang. And in the band was two of the Brunus boys, Henry and Richard. And a clarinet player who played E-flat clarinet instead of the traditional B-flat. His name was Ashil Bakay. And Happy Shilling was in that band. Johnny Fisher. Cack Riley was a trombone player. Henry Brunus was alto horn. And Richie played cornet. And a fellow by the name of Marlow…
Do you know his birth date too, roughly?

items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1967-10-28
items.q: The name of the band that I played with... was called Fishers Ragtime Military Jazz Band... Johnny Fisher. He had a band way back.

ctx.x: Did they call it jazz then?

Yes. The name of the band that I played with, Doug, is funny. It was called Fishers Ragtime Military Jazz Band. Fishers? My father, my father was a drummer, bass drummer in the band. In those days, they used two drums. My father was the bass drummer, and a fellow by the name of Rag Baby Stevens was the snare drummer. And my father built a harness for me so that I could carry the snare drum. And we made this Rex Parade, which was the big carnival parade even then. And Fishers Band was the only band in the parade…
E-flat clarinet's pretty well disappeared these days.
